title: Introduce stubbed tool-adapter playground and auth examples
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a local-first playground demonstrating plugin-style tool adapters, stubbed connectors, and OAuth/ephemeral-credential flows for RAG/agent examples. Recommended for developers testing third-party tool calls without provisioning external services.
description: Motivation: teams frequently need a safe, repeatable way to prototype agents that call external tools (storage, calendars, webhooks, connectors) without setting up real credentials or risking side effects. This PR adds a small, documented playground that: 1) provides a plugin-style 'tool adapter' API for wiring connectors to agents; 2) includes stubbed adapters for S3-like storage, Slack webhook, and Google Drive listing; 3) demonstrates a minimal OAuth/ephemeral-credential exchange shim for local development; 4) wires structured-output contracts and example prompt templates to make tool calls observable in traces and telemetry. What this changes (high level): - new examples/plugin-toolbinding/ directory with 3 example adapters and a lightweight dev server that runs them in-process - docs/examples/toolbinding.md with usage, security considerations, and contract schemas - examples/playgrounds/tool-adapter-replay/ that contains a session recorder/replayer for deterministic dev runs - test/smoke/toolbinding-smoke.sh and a jest-based harness for the adapters - small additions to examples/shared/schema/ for structured-output validators Checklist: - [x] examples and README - [x] smoke tests + CI job - [x] docs pages + crosslinks to authoring guide - [x] explicit guidance on when to replace stubs with real connectors Local quickstart (single continuous command sequence): git checkout feature/plugin-toolbinding-playground && yarn && yarn start:playground Visit http://localhost:3030 to open the playground UI, click 'Create session' to spawn a sandboxed agent with stubbed adapters, and run the sample 'email-extract-and-store' scenario to see tool calls appear in the trace. Security notes: stubs intentionally accept any token in dev mode; docs/examples/toolbinding.md includes production migration steps (KMS, HSM, RBAC, SCIM). Linear/Related: ENG-1832 (playground), PM-412 (dev experience).

notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on the adapter API surface (examples/plugin-toolbinding/playground-server/index.ts) and the structured-output schema. The adapters are intentionally minimal; main risk vectors are credential handling and dangling file descriptors in the replayer.
